questions.question: Delhi Sultanate signifies the rule over India with capital as Delhi, of which community?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Turkish**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Delhi Sultanate** refers to the period of Muslim rule in India from the 13th to the 16th centuries.
 
• The rulers of the Delhi Sultanate were primarily of **Turkish** origin.
 
• It began with the foundation of the **Mamluk Dynasty** by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, who was a former Turkish slave.
 
• The Delhi Sultanate included five dynasties: the **Mamluk (Slave) Dynasty**, the **Khilji Dynasty**, the **Tughlaq Dynasty**, the **Sayyid Dynasty**, and the **Lodi Dynasty**.
 
• These dynasties established and expanded their rule from their capital in **Delhi**.
 
• The Sultanate played a crucial role in the spread of **Islamic culture and architecture** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **African**__

 __
 
• **African** rulers did not establish any long-term sultanate in Delhi.
 
• While Africans did come to India, often as traders or soldiers, they did not rule the Delhi Sultanate.
 
 
 
• **Persian**__
 __
 
• The **Persians** had significant cultural and political influence in India, especially during the Mughal period.
 
• However, the Persian community did not establish the Delhi Sultanate.
 
 
 
• **Arabian**__
 
 
• Although the **Arabs** were the first Muslims to invade India (in the 8th century), they did not establish the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• The Arabian influence was primarily in the Sindh region.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India talks about 'Review of judgments or orders by the Supreme Court'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __137.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ 

__
 
• Article 137 of the Indian Constitution deals with the review of judgments or orders by the Supreme Court.
 
• As per article 137; subject to the provisions of any law made by Parliament or any rules made under article 145, the Supreme Court shall have power to review any judgment pronounced or order made by it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• Article 136: Special leave to appeal by the Supreme Court
 
• (1) Notwithstanding anything in this Chapter, the Supreme Court may, in its discretion, grant special leave to appeal from any judgment, decree, determination, sentence or order in any cause or matter passed or made by any court or tribunal in the territory of India.
 
• (2) Nothing in clause (1) shall apply to any judgment, determination, sentence or order passed or made by any court or tribunal constituted by or under any law relating to the Armed Forces.
 
• Article 138: Enlargement of the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
 
• (1) The Supreme Court shall have such further jurisdiction and powers with respect to any of the matters in the Union List as Parliament may by law confer.
 
• (2) The Supreme Court shall have such further jurisdiction and powers with respect to any matter as the Government of India and the Government of any State may by special agreement confer, if Parliament by law provides for the exercise of such jurisdiction and powers by the Supreme Court.
 
• Article 139: Conferment on the Supreme Court of powers to issue certain writs
 
• Parliament may by law confer on the Supreme Court power to issue directions, orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari, or any of them, for any purposes other than those mentioned in clause (2) of article 32.

questions.question: Who was the man who decrypted the Brahmi script of the Mauryan period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**James Prinsep.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **James Princep** is a British scholar in India, archaeological scientist and migrant officer.
 
• In 1837, James Princep successfully decryed the Brahmi script used in Ashoka inscriptions.
 
• His work on Brahmi script is important in understanding the historical and cultural context of ancient India.
 
• Decrypting the Brahmi has been revealed by the Maurya inscriptions and the emperor Ashoka's kingdom has been given important insights.
 
• His work was a guide for the study of ancient Indian legislative and archaeological science.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmi script:**
 
• The Brahmi script is one of the oldest written systems used in ancient India, which is BC. Belonging to the 3rd century.
 
• It is believed that it is an ancestor of many modern Indian scripts such as Devanagari, Tamil and Bengali.
 
• **Emperor Ashoka**
 
• The third emperor of the Maurya dynasty, Ruled from 268 to 232.
 
• He is famous for Buddhism and Buddhist philosophies such as compassion and non -violence.
 
• Ashoka inscriptions carved on the pillars and rocks are some of the oldest written records in India.
 
• **​Archaeological scientist**
 
• The archaeologist is a person who studies or collect the old objects or things belonging to the past.
 
• James Princep's work as an archaeological scientist has contributed to understanding the ancient Indian history and culture.

questions.question: Which one of the following will be resulted when an animal cell is surrounded by a medium with lower concentration of water?

options.text: No change in movement of water

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 1.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Osmosis:**

 
• It is defined as the **movement of molecules of solvent **from a region of its **higher concentration to a region of its lower concentration **across a semi-permeable membrane.
 
• It is a passive process and happens without any expenditure of energy.
 
• It involves the movement of molecules from a region of higher concentration to lower concentration **until the concentrations become equal** on either side of the membrane.
 
 
• **An isotonic solution** is one that has the same concentration of solutes both inside and outside the cell.
 
• **A hypertonic solution** is one that has a higher solute concentration outside the cell than inside.
 
 
• If the** surrounding has a lower concentration of water **than the cell then w**ater will move by osmosis from the higher concentration (inside the cell) to the lower concentration **(outside the cell) and hence the **cell would lose water.**
 
 
 
• **A hypotonic solution** is one that has a higher solute concentration inside the cell than outside.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png]

__
 
• **In the Tenth Plan period**, the Indian economy grew at **7.7%** per year.
 
• The targeted growth for the **Eleventh Five Year Plan** was **9% per year**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Five Year Plans in India are a centralized and integrated national economic program, and they play a crucial role in guiding the country's economic development.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option:

Statement (A): Tribal communities practiced jhum cultivation as a form of shifting agriculture.

Statement (B): The British encouraged jhum cultivation as it aligned with their economic policies.

Options:

options.text: Both (A) and (B) are true, and (B) is the reason for (A)
Both (A) and (B) are true, but (B) is not the reason for (A)

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is: c) (A) is true, but (B) is false.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement (A): Tribal communities practiced jhum cultivation as a form of shifting agriculture.**

 
 
• This statement is **true**. Jhum cultivation, also known as shifting cultivation, was commonly practiced by tribal communities across different regions in India.
 
• In this agricultural method, a patch of forest is cleared, cultivated for a few years until the soil fertility decreases, and then left fallow as the community moves to a new area.
 
• It was a sustainable form of agriculture adapted to the environmental and cultural needs of many tribal communities.
 
 
 
• **Statement (B): The British encouraged jhum cultivation as it aligned with their economic policies.**
 
 
• This statement is **false**. The British discouraged jhum or shifting cultivation because it did not provide a steady revenue stream, which conflicted with their land revenue policies aimed at maximizing income from agriculture.
 
• The British preferred settled agriculture, which allowed them to impose fixed land taxes, leading them to often ban or restrict shifting cultivation practices, especially in forested regions.
 
 

**Therefore, Statement (A) is true, but Statement (B) is false.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Impact of British Policies on Jhum Cultivation:**__

 
 
• **Restrictions on Shifting Cultivation:** The British imposed various restrictions on jhum cultivation to encourage settled agriculture, which fit their tax collection model better.
 
• **Impact on Tribal Livelihoods:** These restrictions affected tribal communities’ traditional livelihoods, often leading to economic hardship and resistance against British policies.
 
• **Environmental Adaptation:** Jhum cultivation was an eco-friendly practice adapted to the forested and hilly terrains, and its restriction disrupted the ecological balance in some regions.

questions.question: The position when the Earth is farthest from the Sun is known as:
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is Aphelion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Aphelion
 
 
• It is the point of Earth's orbit that is farthest from the Sun.
 
• When the earth reaches aphelion, the sun appears slightly smaller in the sky at any other time of year.
 
• The earth reaches aphelion only once a year.
 
• It happens near of 4th of July.
 
 
 
• Perihelion
 
 
• It is where the Earth is closest to the Sun (91.4 million miles, or 147 million kilometers). 
 
• This occurs around January 3 every year.
 
• The closest point to the Sun in a planet’s orbit is called perihelion. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a5fb2bf1251ae70ac436ce9e42c1f77b56885b837439caf8afe84a8748637927.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Equinox
 
 
• It refers to a day with an equal duration of day and night.
 
• There are two equinoxes in a year:
 
• The entire **earth **experiences equal **day **and equal **night**.
 
• It occurs on the **21st of March** and **September 23rd**.
 
 
 
• Solstice
 
 
• ​It is the time of the year when the sun is farthest from the equatorial giving the long days or nights.
 
• It happens twice a year
 
• Summer Solstice ( June 21)
 
• Winter Solstice( December 22)
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The earth is at the largest distance from the sun (Aphelion point) on the 4th of July.
 
• The Earth is closest to the Sun at its Perihelion about 2 weeks after the December Solstice.
 
• The Earth is farthest from the Sun – at its Aphelion – about 2 weeks after the June Solstice.

questions.question: Which of the following is associated with Atoll?

options.text: It is made up of two mountain chains separated by a large depression
Low islands found in the tropical oceans consisting of coral reefs

Ocean basins with gently sloping terrain

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef** surrounding a central lagoon. 
 
• Atolls are found in** tropical oceans** where the water is warm and clear.
 
• Coral reefs are made up of the skeletons of tiny marine organisms called **coral polyps**. 
 
• Coral polyps secrete a hard substance called **calcium carbonate** that forms the reef structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Mid-ocean ridge: **

 
 
• Mid-ocean ridges are mountain ranges that form at the divergent boundaries of tectonic plates. 
 
• As the plates move apart, magma from the Earth's mantle rises up and cools to form new oceanic crust.
 
 
 
• **Guyot: **
 
 
• Guyots are seamounts with flat tops that have been eroded by waves. 
 
• They are formed when a seamount erupts on the ocean floor and then subsides back into the water.
 
 
 
• **Abyssal plains:**
 
 
• Abyssal plains are the flattest and most common type of ocean floor. 
 
• They are formed by the deposition of sediment from land and from the erosion of seamounts and other underwater features.

questions.question:
What is the correct sequence of the following ports of India from North to South?

A. Kochi port

B. Mormugao port

C. Kandla port

D. Mumbai port
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is: 4 - C, D, B, A**

India's coastline is dotted with several major ports which play a crucial role in the country's trade and commerce. These ports are strategically located along the eastern and western coasts and are essential for the import and export of goods. Understanding the geographical locations of these ports is important for logistics, shipping industry professionals, and students of geography and trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Indian Ports from North to South:

__
 
• Kandla Port (C):

 
 
• Located in the Kutch district of Gujarat in the northwest of India.
 
• One of the major ports on the west coast serving India’s northern and western hinterland.
 
• Known for handling a large volume of cargo including grains, petroleum products, and chemicals.
 
 
 
• Mumbai Port (D):
 
 
• Situated in Maharashtra, on the west coast of India, south of Kandla.
 
• One of the oldest and most significant ports, playing a crucial role in India's maritime trade.
 
• Handles a diverse range of cargo including textiles, chemicals, machinery, and food grains.
 
 
 
• Mormugao Port (B):
 
 
• Located in Goa, further south from Mumbai along the western coastline.
 
• Primarily known for exporting iron ore to Japan, South Korea, China, and European countries.
 
• Also handles coal, petroleum products, and general cargo.
 
 
 
• Kochi Port (A):
 
 
• Situated in Kerala, on the southwest coast of India, making it the southernmost among these ports.
 
• An important port for the southwest region, facilitating trade with the Middle East and Europe.
 
• Handles a variety of cargo, including spices, marine products, and chemicals.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• India’s port sector is regulated and developed by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping, and Waterways.
 
• Major ports are governed by the Indian Ports Act, 1908 and the Major Ports Authorities Act, 2021, which aim to modernize and improve port infrastructure.
 
• Ports play a vital role in facilitating international trade, acting as gateways for import and export activities.
 
• The development of port infrastructure is crucial for economic growth, reducing logistics costs, and boosting trade efficiency.
 
• With ongoing initiatives like the Sagarmala project, the Indian government aims to enhance port connectivity, modernize infrastructure, and promote sustainable coastal development.
